verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents programmatic cluster lifecycle through the CKS API (create, list, update, delete), with token auth, and through a Terraform provider. Once a cluster exists, an agent can get a kubeconfig and run GPU workloads with kubectl or Slurm via SUNK, with the autoscaler scaling GPU Node Pools. However, capacity checks (Capacity Finder) and quota viewing and increase requests are documented as Cloud Console flows, and GPU and workload monitoring is not shown through an API. Missing for 10: an official MCP server or dedicated CLI, an explicit API or CLI path for creating and deleting GPU Node Pools, programmatic GPU health/utilization monitoring, API-based capacity and quota checks, and hands-on corroboration of a fully unattended end-to-end run.
